# Uber M2 — Test Scenarios

Hand-written, dynamic, scenario-driven public test cases. One row per scenario, mapped 1:1 across the 8 themes (see `<Theme>_Tests_Description.md` siblings).

Implementation lives in `emitter/out/Uber_M2/all_public/src/test/java/com/testgen/uber/PublicTests.java`.

| 1   | TC01 — POST registerPath() with a fresh email returns 2xx and a JWT token                                                                                                                               | `public`, `features_m2` | `POST registerPath()` | The §S1-F1 register endpoint must persist a brand-new User account to PostgreSQL and respond with HTTP 2xx plus a body containing a non-blank JWT `token` and a positive `expiresIn` (in milliseconds). Per spec the response shape is `{ "token": "...", "expiresIn": ... }` — no `id` field is returned; chained tests resolve the new user's id from the JWT (`uidFromJwt()`) or via login. | 1) Build a JSON register body with a `nonce()`-suffixed email (e.g., `tc01_<nonce>@grader.testgen.io`), fixed name `"TC01 User"`, a fresh phone string, and a strong password (`TestPwd!2026`).<br>2) POST `/api/users/register` with `Content-Type: application/json` and that body.<br>3) Assert HTTP status is in the 2xx range via `assert2xx`.<br>4) Parse the response body as JSON.<br>5) Assert `token` is non-null and a non-blank string.<br>6) Assert `expiresIn` is present and a positive numeric value. | • HTTP status 200..299<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** Validation rejects a perfectly-valid payload (`@NotBlank` or `@Email` mis-configured), or the persistence path throws and the exception leaks as 5xx (BCrypt encoder not wired, schema column missing, transaction not committing).<br>• Body has non-null `token` field<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** Controller returns `{"id":42}` or an empty body instead of the spec-defined `{token, expiresIn}` envelope — clients have no JWT to authenticate subsequent calls.<br>• `token` is a non-blank string<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** JWT signing wired but emits `""` on a code path (e.g., the secret is read as null and the signer silently produces an empty header.payload.signature triple) — auth filter would later reject every request with that token.<br>• `expiresIn` present and > 0<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** `expiresIn` returned as `0` or omitted — clients have no TTL to manage refresh; usually means the JWT-config Singleton's expiration property was never read. |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 2   | TC02 — Login with valid credentials (happy path)                                                   | `public`, `features_m2`                                                      | `POST registerPath()` (setup), `POST loginPath()`                                                                                                        | The login endpoint (`POST /api/auth/login`) must issue a syntactically-valid JWT when the supplied credentials match a registered user. Checks that the token is exactly three dot-separated segments (`header.payload.signature`) — the canonical compact-serialisation format defined by RFC 7519. Maps to spec S1-F11 (login / token issuance). Common bugs: login issues a plain UUID or opaque string instead of a JWT; the token key in the response body is named differently (e.g., `accessToken`); the token value is blank or null; or the JWT is missing one segment (only two parts, no signature). The setup registers a fresh user so the test is fully self-contained and does not rely on pre-seeded data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | 1) Register a fresh user with `"email":"tc02_<nonce>@grader.testgen.io"` and `"password":"TestPwd!2026"`. Assert 2xx.<br>2) Build login body: `{"email":"<same email>","password":"TestPwd!2026"}`.<br>3) `POST /api/auth/login` with that body.<br>4) Assert login response status is 200–299.<br>5) Parse body; assert `token` field exists and is non-null.<br>6) Assert `token` is a non-blank string.<br>7) Split `token` on `.` and assert exactly 3 segments.                                                                                                                                                                                                        | • Login status 200..299<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: login endpoint not mapped (404) or the auth filter accidentally covers the login path itself, blocking it with 401.<br>• Body has non-blank `token` field<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: response body uses a different key (`accessToken`, `jwt`, `bearerToken`) instead of `token`; or the JWT signing key is null/blank in `application.properties`, causing the service to build an empty token.<br>• Token splits into exactly 3 dot-separated segments (`a.b.c` JWT shape)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: student issues a plain UUID or HMAC-hex string instead of a JWT; or the JWT serialiser omits the signature segment (only 2 parts), meaning no signing is actually happening.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 3   | TC03 — Read own user profile with valid JWT (happy path)                                           | `public`, `updated_crud`                                                     | `POST registerPath()` (setup), `POST loginPath()` (setup), `GET crudReadPath("User")`                                                                    | Validates the full authentication chain end-to-end: the JWT issued by login must be accepted by Spring Security's `OncePerRequestFilter`, the principal extracted from the token must match the path variable `{id}`, and `GET /api/users/{id}` must return the correct user row as a JSON object. Maps to spec S1-F7 (get user by id, with ownership). Tagged `updated_crud` because this CRUD endpoint was updated in M2 to require auth (M1 had no auth). Common bugs: auth filter registered only on `/api/auth/**`, leaving `/api/users/**` unprotected or completely broken; filter parses JWT but does not call `SecurityContextHolder.getContext().setAuthentication()`, causing the ownership check to NPE; or controller returns 403 even for the legitimate owner due to an inverted ownership comparison. Strict `2xx` — **not** the `2xx OR 404` escape — because we registered this exact user moments before; a 404 is a real persistence or filter-chain bug. | 1) Register a fresh user (`tc03_<nonce>@grader.testgen.io`). Assert 2xx. Extract `uid` by decoding the JWT `token` field from the register response and reading the `sub` claim as a Long.<br>2) Login with the same credentials. Assert 2xx. Capture `token`.<br>3) `GET /api/users/<uid>` with header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.<br>4) Assert status is 200–299 (strict — no 404 escape).<br>5) Parse response body; assert it is a JSON object (not an array or primitive).                                                                                                                                                                                        | • GET status 200..299 (strict, **not** the `2xx OR 404` escape)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: JWT filter fails to extract the principal and throws NPE/500; or the filter parses claims but does not write to `SecurityContextHolder`, leaving the controller with an anonymous principal that triggers 401 or 403 even for the legitimate owner.<br>• Response body parses as a JSON object<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: controller returns an empty body (204 No Content), a JSON array (`[]`), or a plain string instead of the user entity object; Jackson serialisation error swallowed as an empty response.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 4   | TC04 — Register with duplicate email returns 4xx (negative path)                                   | `public`, `features_m2`                                                      | `POST registerPath()` (called twice)                                                                                                                     | The register endpoint must enforce email uniqueness and return a `4xx` client error when the same email is submitted a second time. The second request supplies a different `name` and `phone` to confirm uniqueness is keyed on `email` alone. Maps to spec S1-F10 (email uniqueness constraint). Primary bugs caught: `@Column(unique=true)` missing on `User.email` causes the second registration to succeed silently (2xx); an uncaught `DataIntegrityViolationException` from JPA propagates as a 5xx; or a catch block re-throws with a 5xx-range status. Strict `4xx` range assertion (not just "not-2xx") is chosen because the spec requires a client-error response — a 5xx indicates a separate crash bug, not a handled duplicate-email error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | 1) Build payload with `"email":"tc04_<nonce>@grader.testgen.io"` and valid password/phone.<br>2) `POST /api/auth/register` — assert 2xx (precondition: verifies the email is fresh).<br>3) `POST /api/auth/register` **again** with the **same email** but a different name/phone.<br>4) Parse the second response status.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | • First register status 200..299<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: test pre-condition failed — something wrong with the register endpoint before the duplicate attempt.<br>• Second register status 400..499 (strict — must be a client error)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: `@Column(unique=true)` missing on `User.email` — second register creates a duplicate row silently (2xx); or the constraint violation leaks as unhandled `DataIntegrityViolationException` (5xx).<br>• NOT 5xx (no server crash on the duplicate)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: duplicate key exception propagating from JPA through the service as an uncaught runtime exception, producing a 500 Internal Server Error.<br>• NOT 2xx (uniqueness must be enforced)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: email uniqueness constraint missing entirely; two users can share the same email address.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 5   | TC05 — Login with wrong password returns 401 (negative path)                                       | `public`, `features_m2`                                                      | `POST registerPath()` (setup), `POST loginPath()`                                                                                                        | The login endpoint must authenticate the supplied password against the stored BCrypt hash and reject a mismatch with exactly `401 Unauthorized`. Maps to spec S1-F11 (authentication). The assertion ladder is ordered from most-dangerous to most-pedantic bug: a 2xx means password checking was skipped (critical security hole); a 5xx means an unhandled exception leaked; a 404 means the controller leaks account existence (OWASP user-enumeration anti-pattern — when an *existing* user enters the wrong password, the response must be 401, not 404); a 403 is structurally wrong because login is the act of *obtaining* permissions, not *exercising* them. Both passwords differ in prefix and length so BCrypt cannot accidentally match.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 1) Register a fresh user with `"email":"tc05_<nonce>@grader.testgen.io"` and `"password":"TestPwd!2026"`. Assert 2xx.<br>2) Build login body with the **same email** but `"password":"WrongPwd!2026"`.<br>3) `POST /api/auth/login` with that body.<br>4) Assert status is not 2xx, not 5xx, not 404, not 403, and is strictly 401.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | • Register status 200..299 (precondition)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: setup user could not be registered — signals a TC01-level registration bug rather than a login bug; TC05 cannot test its intended scenario.<br>• Login status **strictly 401**<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: any of the four misclassifications — password check skipped (2xx), unhandled exception (5xx), user-enumeration (404), structurally wrong (403).<br>• NOT 2xx (login must reject; would mean no password check)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: `passwordEncoder.matches()` not called — login service returns a token for any password as long as the email exists (critical security vulnerability).<br>• NOT 5xx (server must handle bcrypt mismatch cleanly)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: `BadCredentialsException` or NPE from `passwordEncoder.matches(null, hash)` propagating unhandled from the service as a 500.<br>• NOT 404 (would leak user-enumeration; should be 401 even when account exists)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: login service throws `UserNotFoundException` for the *wrong password* case — the user **exists** but the password is wrong; returning 404 leaks account presence (OWASP anti-pattern).<br>• NOT 403 (login is the act of obtaining permissions, not exercising them)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: controller maps `BadCredentialsException` to `@ResponseStatus(FORBIDDEN)` — 403 is structurally incorrect; login is not the exercise of a privilege. |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

| 7   | TC07 — Missing Authorization header on a non-User CRUD list returns 401 (negative path)            | `public`, `authentication`                                                   | `GET crudCollectionPath(firstTopLevelNonUserEntity())` with NO Authorization header                                                                      | Verifies that the JWT auth filter blocks anonymous requests on non-User CRUD endpoints. The same endpoint as TC06 is used so the two form a clean A/B: TC06 valid-token → 2xx, TC07 no-token → 401. No DB setup is needed because the test exercises whether anonymous requests are blocked before any controller logic runs. Common bugs caught: missing `OncePerRequestFilter` registration; accidental `.permitAll()` on the target controller's URL patterns; or the filter applied only in certain request contexts (e.g., only POST, not GET). The assertion ladder mirrors TC05's order: not-2xx → not-5xx → not-404 → not-403 → strictly-401.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | 1) Resolve the first top-level non-User entity (same as TC06, dynamically determined).<br>2) Build the collection path for that entity.<br>3) `GET <path>` with **no Authorization header** (`httpGet`, not `httpGetAuth`).<br>4) Assert status is not 2xx, not 5xx, not 404, not 403, and is strictly 401.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | • GET status **strictly 401**<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: auth filter not registered, `.permitAll()` on this URL pattern, or filter has a code path that lets anonymous requests through — complete authentication bypass.<br>• NOT 2xx (endpoint wide-open — critical security bug)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: entire service deployed without authentication; any anonymous caller can read all entity collections.<br>• NOT 5xx (filter chain crashed instead of cleanly rejecting)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: NPE in the filter when the `Authorization` header is absent — student calls `header.substring(7)` without first null-checking the header value.<br>• NOT 404 (endpoint reachable without auth — wrong; auth must block FIRST)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: filter passes the request through; controller queries an empty table and returns `[]` with 200, or controller's path is wrong and Spring returns 404 — auth was never checked.<br>• NOT 403 (we sent NO credentials; 403 means "authenticated but lacking permission")<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: student uses `@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")` without an earlier auth gate; Spring resolves an anonymous principal as "authenticated with no roles" and throws `AccessDeniedException` → 403 instead of 401.                                                                                                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 8   | TC08 — Tampered JWT signature is rejected with 401 (negative path)                                 | `public`, `authentication`                                                   | `adminToken()` (setup), `GET crudCollectionPath(firstTopLevelNonUserEntity())` with **tampered** Bearer token                                            | Verifies that the auth filter actually validates the JWT signature, not merely decodes the header and payload. `tamperSignature()` preserves the header and payload of a real token (so it looks structurally valid and passes any "3 segments?" check) but replaces the signature segment with a base64 encoding of `"tampered-signature-does-not-verify"`. A correct HMAC-SHA256 filter rejects this because the expected signature over the original payload does not match. The third leg of the auth-filter triad: TC06 valid → 2xx, TC07 none → 401, **TC08 forged → 401**. Critical bug caught: student calls `Jwts.parserBuilder().build().parseClaimsJwt()` (unsigned variant) instead of `parseSignedClaims()`, trusting payload claims without verifying the signature — enabling anyone to edit the payload (e.g., change role to ADMIN) and re-base64 it without detection.                                                                                      | 1) Call `adminToken()` to get a real, fully-valid admin JWT.<br>2) Call `tamperSignature(token)` — keeps `header.payload` intact but replaces the signature segment with base64(`"tampered-signature-does-not-verify"`).<br>3) Resolve the first top-level non-User entity (same as TC06/TC07, dynamically determined).<br>4) `GET <collection-path>` with header `Authorization: Bearer <tampered-token>`.<br>5) Assert status is not 2xx, not 5xx, not 404, not 403, and is strictly 401.                                                                                                                                                                                 | • GET status **strictly 401**<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: complete JWT signature bypass — student uses the unsigned parser variant (`parseClaimsJwt()`) or decodes the payload with `Base64.decode()` directly; the tampered token is accepted as valid.<br>• NOT 2xx (signature not actually verified — critical security bug)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: anyone can forge tokens by editing the payload and re-encoding it; privilege escalation to ADMIN by hand-editing the role claim is possible.<br>• NOT 5xx (filter chain crashed instead of cleanly rejecting)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: `JwtException` or `SignatureException` during verification is not caught in the filter's try-catch, propagating as an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 401.<br>• NOT 404 (signature mismatch must be caught FIRST)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: filter passes the tampered token through to the controller, which queries for a resource; the query returns nothing and the controller returns 404 — auth was never enforced.<br>• NOT 403 (forged = not-authenticated → 401, not 403)<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;→ Bug it catches: filter catches the `JwtException` but maps it to `AccessDeniedException` instead of `AuthenticationException`, producing 403 instead of the semantically correct 401.                                                                                                                                                                                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 9   | TC09 — Login with non-existent email returns 401 (negative path)                                   | `public`, `features_m2`                                                      | `POST loginPath()` (with email never registered)                                                                                                         | The Uber spec (M2 §10 S1-F11) mandates that the login endpoint returns `401 Unauthorized` for **both** failure cases — "user not found" and "wrong password" — deliberately avoiding `404` to prevent leaking which email addresses are registered (OWASP user-enumeration). This pairs with TC05 (existing user + wrong password → 401) to confirm that the spec's uniform 401-for-all-auth-failures rule is implemented consistently. Common bugs: login service calls `userRepo.findByEmail()` and throws `UserNotFoundException` instead of `BadCredentialsException`, causing a 404 to leak account presence; or the controller maps the not-found condition to 403; or it returns 2xx with a null token, indicating a token was issued for a non-existent user. 403 is structurally wrong here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

| 379 | TC379 — DP-1 Strategy: RefundStrategy interface exists                     | `public`, `patterns`, `strategy`                | (reflection — no HTTP)                                                                       | Per Section 3.2, the Strategy pattern requires a `RefundStrategy` interface with exactly one abstract method named `calculateRefund`. This is the contract every concrete strategy must implement and the entry point the selector dispatches to at runtime. Asserting the interface shape via reflection is the cheapest way to detect a malformed Strategy implementation before exercising any HTTP path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Compiled payment-service classpath available.                  | 1) Reflection-load `RefundStrategy`.<br>2) Assert it is an interface (`Class.isInterface()`).<br>3) Enumerate abstract methods; assert exactly one whose name equals `calculateRefund`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | • RefundStrategy is an interface<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** Strategy modeled as a concrete class or abstract base — defeats polymorphic dispatch.<br>• Exactly one abstract method named calculateRefund<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** Extra abstract methods (e.g., `validate`, `getName`) bloat the contract and force every concrete strategy to override irrelevant methods.                                                                       |
| 380 | TC380 — DP-1 Strategy: 3 concrete strategies implement RefundStrategy      | `public`, `patterns`, `strategy`                | (reflection — no HTTP)                                                                       | Per Section 3.2, the spec mandates three concrete strategies named exactly `FullRefundWithSurgeStrategy`, `BaseFareOnlyRefundStrategy`, and `NoRefundStrategy` (theme.json `s5StrategyFullRefund`/`s5StrategyFoodOnly`/`s5StrategyNoRefund`). Each must implement `RefundStrategy` so the selector can return any of them through the common interface.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | TC379 passes.                                                  | 1) Reflection-load each of the three classes by exact name from theme.json.<br>2) For each, assert `RefundStrategy.class.isAssignableFrom(strategyClass)`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | • All 3 concrete strategy classes load by name<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** Class missing or named differently — selector cannot return the expected type.<br>• Each implements RefundStrategy<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** Class exists but does not implement the interface — won't compile in `selector.select()` return position.                                                                                                                   |
| 381 | TC381 — DP-1 Strategy: RefundStrategySelector exists                       | `public`, `patterns`, `strategy`                | (reflection — no HTTP)                                                                       | Per Section 3.2, the dispatch logic must live in a separate `RefundStrategySelector` (or `RefundStrategyFactory`) class — not in the service. The service should only call `selector.select(payment, request).calculateRefund(...)`. A separate selector keeps the service decoupled from the strategy choice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | None.                                                          | 1) Reflection-scan payment-service classpath for a class named `RefundStrategySelector` or `RefundStrategyFactory`.<br>2) Assert a `select`-like method exists.<br>3) Assert its return type is `RefundStrategy`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | • Selector class exists<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** Selection logic embedded in the service (TC385 catches the consequence; this catches the structural cause).<br>• select() returns RefundStrategy<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;- **Bug it catches:** Method returns a concrete strategy type — defeats polymorphic substitutability and forces the caller to know which strategy ran.                                                                                     |
